subject: Recap: Migration off proprietary LLM APIs — next steps
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Green <sam@brighthealth.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-04T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Recap: Migration off proprietary LLM APIs — next steps

Hi Samantha — great to meet earlier. Short recap from my side and proposed next steps.

Key pain points you raised:
- Cost volatility and rising per-token spend on current OpenAI and Anthropic calls (esp. chat endpoints).
- Vendor lock concerns: model reliability and change management when upstream APIs evolve.
- Latency spikes for peak-workload inference (customer-facing features with <300ms target).

Current stack you described:
- Primary generation: OpenAI Chat API (gpt-4.1x equivalent) for product recommendations.
- Safety/filters: in-house rule engine + Anthropic for assistant moderation.
- Infra: app hosted in GCP us-central1; tokens proxied through a gateway; some caching at edge (Cloud CDN).

Success criteria (what success looks like for BrightHealth):
- 40–60% reduction in per-response inference cost for standard flows while keeping QPS within 10% of today.
- Maintain or improve median latency (target 250–300ms for 512-token workflows).
- No regression on safety/guardrails; audit logs and model provenance available for compliance.

Compatibility and migration constraints you called out:
- Must support existing prompt/response contract (tooling expects ChatMessage schema).
- KV-cache / streaming behavior needs parity for session continuity.
- Prefer models supporting function-like tool calls or structured outputs.

Initial model shortlist we discussed:
- Llama-3 70B quantized (fast path for high throughput)
- Mistral Instruct variants (good cost/quality balance)
- Redmond-open-compat (Redwood-curated 1-shot compatible variant)

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive (SE call): Neha to run workload replay sample — please share a 24–48h traffic capture and 10 representative prompts.
2) Cost/latency projection: we will send a short model comparison matrix with estimated unit costs.
3) Security/compliance: send SOC2 evidence and data flow diagram to your security team.
4) SOW ask: you flagged procurement timelines — I attached a draft SOW and a migration checklist for internal review.

Can you confirm the two items you promised on the call: 1) the sample prompt set and 2) the rough committed QPS target for launch?

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com | (415) 555-0199

Subject: Re: Recap: Migration off proprietary LLM APIs — next steps

Thanks for the recap, Jonas — that aligns well. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Prompt set: we can share anonymized examples (PHI stripped) — target to deliver by Monday EOD (2026-08-10).
- QPS: baseline is ~18 qps during business hours, headroom up to 60 qps for peak tests. For launch we expect to commit ~30 qps.
- Safety: our moderation stack is non-negotiable; we need an evaluation plan that demonstrates parity with Anthropic moderation today.

Two questions: 1) do you have an expected downtime window for cutover? 2) regarding licensing — are there any per-seat or per-host fees outside of token/compute?

I'll loop in Procurement (Luis) to start timeline discussions — he may have follow-ups about contracts and data residency.

Best,
Samantha Green
Head of Product, BrightHealth AI
sam@brighthealth.ai

Samantha — quick answers inline and next actions.

Downtime/cutover: we recommend a staged cutover with feature flags and dark launches; objective is zero-customer-visible downtime. For full DNS/path cutover we typically see a brief (<90s) traffic switch while caches warm. We will provide a migration runbook.

Licensing: Redwood's hosted offering is usage-first (per-token + per-embedding). For Dedicated/Private deployments there are committed capacity contracts; no per-seat fees. If you require an on-prem package we can scope a platform license + support tier. We'll put details in the SOW.

Neha (cc'd) — can you pick an initial 24h sample replay window and run a quick baseline against the Mistral and Llama-3 quantized configs? Ideally we get latency percentiles and token cost deltas.

Next actions (owners & ETA):
- BrightHealth: share anonymized prompts and target commit QPS (Samantha) — ETA 2026-08-10
- Redwood SE: replay and small-scale perf matrix (Neha) — ETA 2026-08-07
- Redwood Sales: send cost projection and updated SOW (Jonas) — ETA 2026-08-06 (attached draft SOW)

If that timeline works I'll put a 60-min technical slot on Thursday for the replay results review.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com

Jonas / Samantha — Procurement here. Two quick items from legal/procurement POV: 

1) Data residency: BrightHealth requires all inference and logging for PHI-stripped PII to remain in US regions only. We need a clause in the contract confirming region locking and auditability.
2) SLA & credits: please provide the standard uptime SLA and an example credit schedule for P0/P1 incidents.

I'll review the draft SOW and provide redlines by Friday EOD. Please attach the SOC2 report and the list of subcontractors that will have access to logs.
